hypotheses.statement: For standard Solidity 0.8 checked-arithmetic failures and require(string)/assert, solang reproduces solc's ABI-encoded revert payloads: require(false, "msg") decodes to the same reason string, and assert/division-by-zero/underflow/array-OOB/negative-int-cast all decode to the same Panic(uint256) codes (0x01, 0x12, 0x11, 0x32, 0x21) on both toolchains after SCALE decoding.

evidence.note: All 5 revert variants (require string, assert, div/0, uint underflow, array OOB, int8->uint8 negative cast) produced matching decoded revert reasons across both toolchains; okStore + count query + events also matched.

Boundary cases of Error(string) encoding matched exactly: empty-string revert/require, short ASCII, and a 78-byte UTF-8 string all decoded identically; custom errors with args (MyErr(42, sender)) and no args (EmptyErr()) produced matching selectors and ABI-decoded arguments on both toolchains. h1's predicted agreement holds across the full revert-payload surface tested.

hypotheses.next_probe: Test boundary cases of Error(string) encoding: revert with an empty string, a string longer than 32/64 bytes with non-ASCII (UTF-8) bytes, and custom errors with parameters (e.g. error MyErr(uint256 code, address who)), comparing decoded selector, args, and string bytes between solc/anvil and solang/pallet-contracts.

hypotheses.statement: Revert payload agreement extends beyond top-level calls: reverts thrown inside constructors (deploy-time failures) and reverts caught via try/catch on external calls are surfaced with identical ABI-encoded payloads on solc/anvil and solang/pallet-contracts, including the receiver side of low-level calls returning returndata.

evidence.note: All top-level revert encodings (empty/UTF-8 strings, custom errors with/without args) matched; untested surfaces are constructor reverts and try/catch payload decoding.

hypotheses.next_probe: Probe a contract whose constructor reverts with require(cond, "ctor fail") and a custom error, plus a caller contract using try/catch over an external call that reverts with Error(string) and Panic(0x11); compare deployment failure reasons and the decoded catch-block payloads (including catch (bytes memory data)) between both toolchains.
